newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says trade fair proves U.S. ban failure.
newsitem.headline: Iran says trade fair proves U.S. ban failure.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani opened Tehran's annual international fair on Tuesday, saying a wider turnout by foreign firms showed U.S. sanctions against Iran had failed.
"The extensive presence of many industrial countries here conveys the sweet message that American bullying and monopolistic attitudes are not heeded," Tehran radio quoted Rafsanjani as saying.
Some 1,500 foreign companies from 54 countries were taking part in the eight-day fair, up from the 800 firms from 53 states that attended the event last year, Iranian media said.
The number of companies from Germany, France, Italy and England was up 30 percent, the media reports said.

Iranian officials have welcomed opposition by European Union members and other states against a United States law approved in August that punishes non-U.S. firms investing $40 million or more in Iran's gas and oil industries.
Some 2,500 Iranian firms were taking part in the fair, part of Iran's efforts to boost fledgling non-oil exports.
Crude oil comprises about 80 percent of Iran's exports.

Non-oil exports, dominated by traditional products such as Persian carpets and pistachios, fell about 25 percent in the Iranian year that ended on March 19, 1996 due to tough foreign exchange rules adopted in May 1995.
Under the new rules, Iran banned free currency exchange, setting a fixed rate of 3,000 rials to the dollar and told exporters to exchange their hard cash income at the official rate in state banks.
The move was aimed at boosting the value of the Iranian currency, which fell to as low as 7,000 to the dollar after the announcement of a U.S. trade and investment ban on Iran.
The United States accuses Iran of sponsoring terrorism and seeking to develop nuclear arms. Tehran denies both charges.
